guide.summary: Private app, own paid workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public app, installable by any customer (app review, wait up to 7 business days per submission).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, own paid workspace only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app, installable by any customer (app review, wait up to 7 business days per submission).

composio.note: Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. For launch with your own branding, use your own app's client ID and secret in a Composio auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototyping, since Composio provides a managed Intercom app. For production you will likely want your own app for your branding on the consent screen and a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio's
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Default scopes may not match what you need

prerequisites.title: Intercom developer account and paid workspace
prerequisites.detail: You need a developer account, and any use of Intercom itself requires Intercom's Customer Agreement. Private apps need a paid workspace.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and end user agreement
prerequisites.detail: You must present a privacy policy to end users, compatible with Intercom's terms. Listing also needs terms, privacy, docs and support URLs.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register several, so test and production can both be added.

prerequisites.title: Test account for reviewers
prerequisites.detail: If your app needs an account or subscription, give Intercom test credentials or setup instructions in the description.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with managed app
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Intercom app to prototype while your own app is in review.
steps.done_when: A test user can connect Intercom through Composio.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: Log in to the Developer Hub, create the app and tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page. Copy the client ID and secret from Basic Information.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Pick minimal scopes and add redirect URL
steps.detail: Draft the smallest scope list that covers the agent's tools, with a justification for each. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Scopes and HTTPS redirect URL are saved in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with own credentials
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API using your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works on your dev workspace.

steps.title: Prepare the demo video script
steps.detail: Script a video showing OAuth install with full client_id and state in the URL, all app functionality, and OAuth uninstall.

steps.title: Record the video and complete listing pages
steps.detail: Record the video, then fill in the App Listing and App Partner Program pages with images, URLs and company details.
steps.done_when: All pages in Test and publish show complete.

steps.title: Submit app for review
steps.detail: Submit from the Test and publish section.
steps.done_when: Developer Hub shows the review banner.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Documented as up to seven business days. If changes are requested, fix and resubmit.

steps.title: Generate access token for own workspace
steps.detail: Create a private app and generate the access token in the Intercom dashboard.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes are the top rejection reason
traps.detail: Request only the scopes the agent uses. Intercom may also approve fewer scopes than requested, limiting your credentials.

traps.title: Unclear links or incomplete video cause rejection
traps.detail: Broken installation links cause rejection. A video that misses functionality or OAuth flows must be resubmitted.

traps.title: Each resubmission restarts the wait
traps.detail: Resubmissions can take up to seven business days again. A 2021 forum post reports no response after 15 days.

traps.title: Intercom can refuse or withdraw approval
traps.detail: Approval is at Intercom's sole discretion, and Intercom has no duty to list your app. It may revoke credentials if a re-review finds non-compliance.

traps.title: Naming and branding rules
traps.detail: App name cannot contain Intercom and must be 40 characters or less. The icon cannot contain the Intercom logo.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see Composio on the consent screen and share quota with all Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Review asks you to adjust scopes and resubmit
blockers.what_it_means: Requested scopes go beyond the app's current functionality.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove unused scopes, explain the rest, and resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare scopes against the agent's actual API calls and draft the justification.

blockers.symptom: Video rejected and must be resubmitted
blockers.what_it_means: It did not show all functionality and the OAuth processes.
blockers.what_to_do: Re-record to show install, all features, and uninstall.
blockers.agent_can_help: Write a checklist script of everything to show.

open_questions: Real-world review time is unclear: official doc says up to 7 business days, a 2021 forum post reports 15 days. Ask Intercom support via Messenger for current timing.
Which scopes an AI agent needs is not specified by the docs. Map each Composio tool to Intercom API endpoints and check the scope list in Developer Hub.
Whether customer workspace admins must approve installs is not stated; the docs mention only the end user approving. Test a connection with a second workspace.

evidence.answer: A developer forum report (March 2021) describes an app still unreviewed 15 days after submission, with no response from support; the thread title refers to a 14-day review window.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: We are currently in the review of our app and we got some confusing suggestions to our app review that does not quite make sense for our app and it's capabilities.
evidence.answer: A developer forum report (March 2021) says review feedback seemed confusing; an Intercom employee replied that the Support team handles app reviews and developers should contact them via Messenger, with no direct reviewer contact offered.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: You will see a yellow banner at the top of the screen stating it can take up to seven business days for review.
evidence.answer: Official doc (not a developer report): Intercom states review can take up to seven business days.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Providing broken or unclear links will result in an application rejection, and you will have to resubmit for review.
evidence.answer: Common blocker stated in the official doc: broken or unclear installation links cause rejection and a resubmission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: If you have requested scopes outside of the current functionality, you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app.
evidence.answer: Common blocker stated in the official doc: requesting scopes beyond what the app actually uses can lead to a request to adjust scopes and resubmit.
